summary: One blocker: the TikZ fix introduces spaces into ordinary grouped prose, allowing banned words and copied 12-word passages to escape detection. The original round 1 cases are addressed by inspection. All five checks remain NOT_RUN as instructed.

checks.criterion: AC1: Shared LaTeX-to-prose extraction preserves prose and source lines.
checks.evidence: Both consumers use tex_prose.extract, but paper/scripts/tex_prose.py:560 inserts a space at every adjacent group boundary. For example, \emph{{seam}{less}} becomes 'seam less' although its prose is 'seamless'.

checks.criterion: AC2: Linter scans the required files, reports findings and fails without rule-disable options.
checks.evidence: Static inspection: paper/scripts/tex_prose.py:226 recursively selects .tex files and excludes only figures/styles.tex. paper/scripts/lint_prose.py:115 formats findings; :246 exposes only --root; :261 prints findings and returns 1 when any exist.

checks.criterion: AC3: All six prose rules enforce the specified behavior.
checks.evidence: paper/scripts/lint_prose.py:157 matches banned words against extracted prose. The space introduced at paper/scripts/tex_prose.py:560 lets \emph{{seam}{less}} evade the seamless rule and can similarly split words within the forbidden phrase.

checks.criterion: AC4: Normalized abstract-overlap detection rejects every shared run of at least 12 tokens.
checks.evidence: paper/scripts/overlap_check.py:118 tokenizes the altered extraction. Against the abstract in test_overlap_check.py:25, 'We measure the roughness of \emph{{lu}{nar}} and martian terrain at baselines from' splits lunar into two tokens and hides the otherwise shared 12-word run.

checks.evidence: Static inspection: tex_prose.py:402 preserves TikZ contents while blanking comments; lint_prose.py:216 supplies that extraction to both word rules. test_tex_prose.py:252 and test_lint_prose.py:359 assert command-argument and math cases. The separate grouping regression is reported below.
The listed implementation commits touch only the nine scoped product files. scripts/ralph/prompt.md:21 permits the batch story list and progress log; :36 permits review-resolution bookkeeping.

lint_prose.py:104 recognizes bounded bold commands, and :205 excludes tabular spans. Rejecting a bare \bf declaration is consistent with the prohibition on bold prose; the rebuttal does not weaken that rule.

findings.claim: The TikZ repair inserts word boundaries into ordinary grouped prose, allowing both mandatory prose guards to be bypassed.
findings.evidence: Static trace, not executed: _prose unconditionally replaces every '}{' boundary with a space. Consequently, \emph{{seam}{less}} extracts as 'seam less' and escapes banned_word_hits. Against the existing test abstract, 'We measure the roughness of \emph{{lu}{nar}} and martian terrain at baselines from' renders the same 12 words but extracts 'lu nar', breaking overlap detection at overlap_check.py:118. Preserve ordinary TeX group adjacency and handle TikZ argument separation with appropriate context; add regression assertions for both consumers.

resolution.reason: Fixed in 2d9f03f, with failing tests first in b4fdff0. Pass 2 no longer reads every }{ as a word break. _CodeScanner.argument_breaks() marks a break only between two arguments of one command. argument_count() gives the count: one for formatting commands, accents and begin/end; none for declarations such as \bf, \small and \item; for key commands, their keys plus the text arguments listed in TEXT_ARGUMENTS_AFTER_KEYS (\textcolor 2, \multirow 3); every following group for an unknown command, whose definition is not known. Before each argument the scan skips what TeX skips (space_end, read in the source) and optional [..] arguments. Ordinary groups now join as TeX prints them: \emph{{seam}{less}}, {seam}{less}, \emph{sea}{mless}, {\bf pivo}{tal} and \bf{seam}{less} read as one word. The round 1 TikZ cases still split: \textcolor{pivotal}{x}, \textcolor[rgb]{1,0,0}{pivotal}, \newterm{a}{b}. New regressions for both consumers: test_tex_prose.py (13 plain and 4 kept-TikZ cases), test_lint_prose.py (banned-word in prose and TikZ, and important-to-note with \emph{{impor}{tant}}), and test_overlap_check.py (your example, \emph{{lu}{nar}}, and {lu}{nar} within 12 abstract words). 23 of them failed before the fix. All five story checks pass, with 609 tests.
